summary.plain: MINERvA reports what it describes as, to its knowledge, the first high-statistics measurement of an antineutrino scattering off a free proton (hydrogen) rather than a proton bound inside a heavier nucleus, and extracts the nucleon's axial charge radius: 0.73 ± 0.17 femtometres.
summary.technical: To the authors' knowledge the first high-statistics measurement of the ν̄μp→μ⁺n cross-section on hydrogen, using the plastic-scintillator target of MINERvA; it extracts the nucleon axial form factor F_A(Q²) from free proton targets, without the nuclear corrections that neutrino-deuterium extractions require, and gives the nucleon axial charge radius r_A = 0.73 ± 0.17 fm.

title: Measurement of the axial vector form factor from antineutrino–proton scattering
why_it_matters: The abstract says the axial form factor had so far been extracted from neutrino-deuterium scattering, which requires uncertain nuclear corrections; the antineutrino-hydrogen scattering presented here can access it without the need for nuclear theory corrections and enables direct comparisons with lattice quantum chromodynamics computations.
